terms.gloss: suspected; as a noun, a suspect
evidence: Ter. Hec. 4.2.1: tibi mē esse suspectam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The person who suspects is in the dative (suspectus rēgī, Sall. Jug. 70.1); the crime in the genitive (suspectus sceleris, Curt.) or with in (in morte mātris, Suet. Vit. 14). Suspectum habēre aliquem, to suspect someone (Plaut. Bacch.). Traupman uses suspectus, suspectī m. as a noun, “a suspect”.

terms.grammar: phrase: a relative clause with suspīciō, suspīciōnis f.

phrases.latin: nōn clam mē est, tibi mē esse suspectam
phrases.english: I am well aware that you suspect me

phrases.latin: Bomilcar suspectus rēgī et ipse eum suspiciēns
phrases.english: Bomilcar, suspected by the king and suspecting him in turn

sources: Lewis & Short: suspicio · Lewis & Short: suspectus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 197, 388, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
